extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for recording examiner-applicant interviews and for making amendments to U.S. patent applications under 37 CFR 1.121 and related MPEP sections. Covers what must be included in interview summaries, who may participate, handling of exhibits/demonstrations, and detailed amendment presentation rules for specification, claims, and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and proper recordation of interview substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete and proper recordation of the substance of any interview should include at least the following applicable items:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) a brief description of the nature of any exhibit shown or any demonstration conducted; (B) identification of the claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of the principal proposed amendments of a substantive nature discussed, unless already described on the Interview Summary form; (E) identification of the general principal thrust arguments of the applicant and the examiner (need not be verbatim or highly detailed; identification sufficient if general nature/thrust is understandable in file context); (F) a general indication of any other pertinent matters discussed; (G) if appropriate, the general results or outcome of the interview; (H) for interviews via electronic mail, a paper copy of the e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the file as required by the Federal Records Act in the same manner as Examiner Interview Summary Form, PTOL 413. The Interview Summary form will not be considered complete and proper unless it includes or is supplemented to include all applicable items above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review and correction of interview record
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to carefully review the applicant’s record of the substance of an interview for completeness and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record is not complete or accurate, the examiner may give the applicant a 1-month time period (or 30 days from mailing date, whichever is longer) under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to complete the reply when the record is in a reply to a nonfinal Office action. If an inaccuracy bears directly on patentability, it should be pointed out in the next Office letter. If the record is complete and accurate, the examiner should mark 'Interview record OK' on the paper recording with date and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on interviews after appeal brief or after passed to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the brief on appeal is filed or after an application has been passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be appropriate before applicant’s first reply if allowable subject matter is present or to help applicant judge whether to continue prosecution. Requests for interviews after notice of allowance should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority required to participate in interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are generally not granted to persons who lack proper authority from the applicant or attorney/agent of record; a mere power to inspect is not sufficient authority for granting an interview involving the merits of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office employees are forbidden to hold oral or written communication with an unregistered, suspended, or excluded attorney/agent regarding an application unless that person is the applicant. Registered individuals who are local representatives of the attorney generally need a power of attorney or Authorization to Act in a Representative Capacity on file. Under 37 CFR 10.57(c) a practitioner cannot authorize other registered practitioners to conduct interviews without client consent after full disclosure; a practitioner cannot authorize a nonpractitioner to conduct interviews (37 CFR 10.47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone/email/video interviews and authority documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For telephone interviews, a facsimile transmission of a power of attorney is recommended prior to the interview; otherwise the examiner may conduct the telephone interview with the Office file closed and work solely from the practitioner's file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone, electronic mail, or video conference interviews may be used for remote parties. Present Office policy emphasizes telephone interviews initiated by the examiner to attorneys/agents of record. If the practitioner is authorized but not of record, faxed power of attorney is recommended to enable discussion from the Office file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews should only be granted to parties with binding authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews normally should not be granted unless the requesting party has authority to bind the principal concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that any agreements or concessions made in the interview can be relied upon during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include examiner with negotiation authority when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: For an interview with an examiner who does not have negotiation authority, arrangements should always include an examiner who does have such authority and who is familiar with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows authoritative agreement to be reached at the time of the interview and avoids delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouped interviews practice for remote applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouped interviews are effective for attorneys remote from the Washington, D.C. area who prefer personal or video conference interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prearranged interview includes agreement to file a prompt supplemental amendment putting the case nearly in condition for concluding action, prompt filing gives the application special status and brings it up for immediate special action.

rubrics_metrics.name: No discussion of inter partes questions ex parte
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits ex parte discussion of issues that are part of inter partes proceedings to preserve fairness and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure of other cases during interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview in the examiner’s room, the examiner should arrange the desk so that all files, drawings and other papers, except those necessary in the interview, are placed out of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents inadvertent exposure of other applicants' confidential information; see MPEP § 101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling demonstrations, exhibits, and models
rubrics_metrics.description: Models or exhibits may be exhibited or demonstrated during the interview, but a model or exhibit will not generally be admitted as part of the record unless it complies with 37 CFR 1.91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the model/exhibit is merely used for demonstration, it will not be made part of the record; a full description of what was demonstrated/exhibited must be made of record per 37 CFR 1.133(b). Exhibits too large for the Office may be viewed by the examiner outside the Office with supervisory approval. It is presumed that witnessing a demonstration or reviewing an exhibit is essential to developing/clarifying issues in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection — restrictions and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally one interview after final rejection is permitted, but the intended purpose and content of the interview should be presented briefly, preferably in writing, prior to the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview after final may be granted if the examiner is convinced that disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews merely to restate arguments of record or to discuss new limitations which would require more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied. A second or further interview after final may be held if examiner is convinced it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews involving cases sent to issue (post-allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue (37 CFR 1.312), an interview involving detailed consideration of claims sought to be entered and discussion of prior art to determine allowability should not be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is not entitled to greater consideration informally than when formally presented; requests for interviews after a notice of allowance should be granted only with Technology Center Director approval and a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments filed on or after July 30, 2003 must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 as revised; if an amendment does not comply, the Office will notify applicants via a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment that the amendment is not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revision facilitates electronic image processing. The Manner of making amendments is summarized, and non-compliant papers will receive a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment sections and document structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section of an amendment document (e.g., Specification Amendments, Claim Amendments, Drawing Amendments, and Remarks) must begin on a separate sheet to facilitate indexing and electronic scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended amendment paper format (order): (A) cover sheet/table of contents with application info; (B) 'Amendments to the Specification' (separate sheet); (C) 'Amendments to the Claims' including complete listing of all claims ever presented; (D) 'Amendments to the Drawings'; (E) remarks section (separate sheet); (F) any drawings being submitted including Replacement/New/Annotated sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification (other than claims, computer listings, sequence listings) must be made by adding, deleting or replacing a paragraph, by replacing a section, or by a substitute specification, and must unambiguously identify the location to be modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For paragraph amendments: (i) an instruction identifying location; (ii) full text of replacement paragraph(s) with markings showing changes relative to previous version; added subject matter shown by underlining; deleted matter shown by strike-through (double brackets may be used for five or fewer chars); (iii) full text of any added paragraphs presented without underlining (clean); (iv) deleted paragraph text must not be presented with strike-through or double brackets. If paragraph numbering present, replacement paragraphs should keep or extend numbering (e.g., [0071], [0071.1]). A deleted paragraph can only be reinstated by a subsequent amendment adding the previously deleted paragraph or section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement section and substitute specification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment by replacement section requires a reference to the section heading and a replacement section with markings to show all changes; substitute specifications require compliance with 37 CFR 1.125(b) & (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up replacement section: added subject matter underlined; deleted matter strike-through (double brackets for small deletions or if strike-through not clear). Substitute specification requires a clean version, a separate marked-up version showing changes relative to prior version, and a statement that the substitute specification contains no new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amendment — complete claim listing and status identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendment document that includes any change to a claim, cancellation of a claim, or addition of a claim must include a complete listing of all claims ever presented in the application, with the status of every claim indicated after its claim number by one of the specified identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status identifiers: (Original), (Currently amended), (Canceled), (Withdrawn), (Previously presented), (New), (Not entered). Claims listing shall be in ascending numerical order. Consecutive claims with status 'canceled' or 'not entered' may be aggregated (e.g., Claims 1–5 (canceled)). The claim listing commences on a separate sheet and sheets containing claim text shall not contain other amendment parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims markings and presentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims being currently amended must be presented with markings to indicate the changes relative to the immediate prior version: strike-through for deleted matter and underlining for added matter, with limited exceptions for double brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) deletion of five or fewer consecutive characters may use double brackets (e.g., [[eroor]]); (2) if strike-through cannot be easily perceived (e.g., deletion of number '4'), double brackets must be used (e.g., [[4]]). An alternative technique is to include extra text before/after the deletion in strike-through followed by underlining of the desired change. An accompanying clean version is not required and should not be presented. Only claims with status 'currently amended' or 'withdrawn' (if also being amended) shall include markings. Claims added by amendment must be indicated as 'new' and the text must not be underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims clean version and assertion of no change
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of all pending claims not being currently amended shall be presented in the claim listing in clean version (without markings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of a clean version of any claim having the status 'original', 'withdrawn', or 'previously presented' constitutes an assertion that it has not been changed relative to the immediate prior version, except to omit prior markings. Any claim added by amendment must be indicated 'new' and presented in clean version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation and reinstatement of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No claim text shall be presented for any claim in the claim listing with the status of 'canceled' or 'not entered'; cancellation is effected by instruction to cancel a particular claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation may be indicated by listing claim number and status identifier only. A previously canceled claim can only be reinstated by adding the claim as a 'new' claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing amendment presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to application drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and be submitted on a replacement sheet labeled 'Replacement Sheet' in the top margin; replacement sheet shall include all figures appearing on immediate prior version of the sheet even if only one figure is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new sheet with an additional figure must be labeled 'New Sheet'. All changes to drawings must be explained in detail in the drawing amendment or remarks section. A marked-up copy (Annotated Sheet) including annotations indicating changes may be included and must be clearly labeled when provided. A marked-up copy must be provided when required by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be required to ensure the specification, claims, and drawings substantially correspond; this is an affirmative Office requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits adding subject matter beyond the original disclosure; substitute specifications must include a statement that no new matter is being introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner's amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, including the claims, made by the Office in an examiner’s amendment may be made by specific instructions to insert or delete subject matter set forth in the examiner’s amendment by identifying the precise point in the specification or the claim(s) where the insertion or deletion is to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with certain formatting paragraphs (e.g., 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1), (b)(2), or (c)) is not required for examiner's amendments when they are implemented as specific instructions by the Office.
